Usage And Examples ### `ContextMenuView` Example 01 **Summary**: A basic context menu that has 3 menu action items (e.g. "Action #1", "Action #2", and "Action #3").
| Notes | | :----------------------------------------------------------- | | 1️⃣ — The `ContextMenuView.menuConfig` prop accepts an optional `MenuConfig` object.
This object will be used to create and configure the context menu. | | 2️⃣ — You can set the context menu title via passing a string value to the `MenuConfig.menuTitle` property.

📝 **Note**: You can pass an empty string if you don't want a title to appear on top your context menu. | | 3️⃣ — To populate the context menu with action items, you can pass a `MenuActionConfig` object in the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property.

📝 **Note A**: The `MenuConfig.menuItems` property can accept an array of a `MenuElementConfig` union type.

To be more specific, the `menuItems` property can accept an array containing any of the following object types: `MenuConfig` object, `MenuActionConfig`, and `DeferredMenuElementConfig`.

📝 **Note B**: If you pass in a `MenuConfig` object in the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property, it means that you want to create a submenu. See [`ContextMenuView` Example 03](#ContextMenuView-Example-03) for more details.

📝 **Note C**: If you pass in a `DeferredMenuElementConfig` object in the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property, it means that you want to create a deferred menu item (i.e. a menu item that has a loading indicator). See [`ContextMenuView` Example 19](#ContextMenuView-Example-19) for more details. | | 4️⃣ — A `MenuActionConfig` object represents an action item in the context menu (e.g. copy, paste, delete, etc).

As such, if you pass in a `MenuActionConfig` object to `MenuConfig.menuItems`, it means that you want to create a context menu action.

📝 **Note A**: The `MenuActionConfig.actionKey` property serves as a unique identifier for your menu action. If you have multiple menu actions, the `actionKey` will help you differentiate them.

📝 **Note B**: You will receive the value you passed in `MenuActionConfig.actionKey` in the `ContextMenuView.onPressMenuItem` event (i.e. via the `nativeEvent` object). | | 5️⃣ — You can use the `ContextMenuView.onPressMenuItem` event prop to get notified whenever a menu action item has been selected.

The function you pass to the `onPressMenuItem` prop will receive a `OnPressMenuItemEventObject` object.

📝 **Note A**: Details about the selected menu action item can be accessed via the `OnPressMenuItemEventObject.nativeEvent` object.

E.g. `OnPressMenuItemEventObject``.nativeEvent.actionKey`.

📝 **Note B**: If `ContextMenuView.shouldWaitForMenuToHide`
`BeforeFiringOnPressMenuItem` prop is set to `true` (which it is by default), then this event will fire after the `onMenuDidHide` event is triggered. |
[🔗 Full Example](./example/src/examples/ContextMenuViewExample01.tsx) ```jsx // 📝 Note: for the sake of brevity, some of the code is omitted... import { ContextMenuView } from 'react-native-ios-context-menu'; export function ContextMenuViewExample01(props) { return ( { Alert.alert( 'onPressMenuItem Event', `actionKey: ${nativeEvent.actionKey} - actionTitle: ${nativeEvent.actionTitle}` ); }} > {/** Components */} ); }; ``` ![screenshot](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample01-old.png) ![Gif](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample01.gif)
### `ContextMenuView` Example 02 **Summary**: Icon Example — This examples shows how to add a system icon in the context menu action.
| Notes | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1️⃣ — A menu action (i.e. `MenuActionConfig` object) can be configured to show an icon via its `MenuActionConfig.icon` property.

📝 **Note A**: The `icon` property accepts a `ImageItemConfig` object.

📝 **Note B**: A `ImageItemConfig` object is used to describe images/assets (e.g. SF Symbols icons, images, xcasset images, programmatic images, etc). | | 2️⃣ — In this example, we want to use a "SF Symbols" icon for the menu action.

In order to do this, the `ImageItemConfig.type` property must be set to `"IMAGE_SYSTEM"`.

📝 **Note A**: Passing in a value of `"IMAGE_SYSTEM"` to the `type` property means that we want to create a "SF Symbols" system icon.

📝 **Note B**: Using a "SF Symbols" icon requires iOS 13+.

📝 **Note C**: Via the `ImageItemConfig` object, you can also configure the context menu action to use other icons (e.g. `xcasset` items, images, gradients, solid colors, etc).

📝 **Note D**: You can apply a tint to the icon via the `ImageItemConfig.imageOptions` property using the `UIImageConfig.tint` and `UIImageConfig.renderingMode` property. See [`ContextMenuView` Example 17](#ContextMenuView-Example-17) for more details. | | 3️⃣ — In order to configure what kind of "SF Symbols" icon we want to use for the menu action, we need to pass in a `ImageSystemConfig` object to the `ImageItemConfig.imageValue` property.

We can set what kind of icon to use via passing a string value to the `ImageSystemConfig.systemName` property.

📝 **Note A**: An `ImageSystemConfig` object is used to generate a "SF Symbols" image. Using this configuration object, we can optionally customize the "SF Symbols" icon further via the following properties: `pointSize`, `weight`, `scale`, `hierarchicalColor`, `paletteColors`, etc.

📝 **Note B**: The string value passed to the `ImageSystemConfig.systemName` property must be a valid SF Symbols name.

📝 **Note C**: To view the list of SF Symbols icons (along with their corresponding icon names), you'll need to download the SF Symbols Mac app from [this page](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sf-symbols/overview/). |
[🔗 Full Example](./example/src/examples/ContextMenuViewExample02.tsx) ```jsx // 📝 Note: for the sake of brevity, some of the code is omitted... import { ContextMenuView } from 'react-native-ios-context-menu'; export function ContextMenuViewExample02(props) { return ( {/** Components */} ); }; ``` ![screenshot](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample02-old.png) ![Gif](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample02.gif)
### `ContextMenuView` Example 03 **Summary**: Nested Menu — This example shows a context menu that has a submenu item inside its list of menu actions.
| Notes | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1️⃣ — A context menu supports having nested menu's (i.e. submenu's).

A submenu is basically just another menu with it's own separate list of menu actions. Tapping it will show another context menu (visually this is similar to a dropdown menu). | | 2️⃣ — As mentioned in the earlier examples, the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property can accept a `MenuActionConfig` object, or a `MenuConfig` object.

Passing in a `MenuActionConfig` object to `MenuConfig.menuItems` makes a menu action, conversely passing in a `MenuConfig` object will create a submenu item.

In other words, to make a submenu, you just need to pass a `MenuConfig` item in the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property.

📝 **Note**: You can nest as many submenu's you want (but just remember that having more than 3 nested submenus is considered bad UX). |

### `ContextMenuView` Example 04 **Summary**: Menu Attributes — This example context menu showcases the `MenuActionConfig.menuAttributes` property.
| Notes | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1️⃣ — The `MenuActionConfig.menuAttributes` property accepts an array of strings (i.e. an array of `MenuAttributes` items).

In this example, the context menu has 3 actions, each with a different menu attribute assigned to it.

The first menu action is a "disabled" action, i.e. it has it's `menuAttributes` set to `['disabled']`, causing the action title text and icon becomes greyed out. | | 2️⃣ — The second menu action is a destructive action.

It has it's `menuAttributes` set to `['destructive']`, causing the action title text and icon becomes red. | | 3️⃣ — The third menu action is a "hidden" action. It has it's `menuAttributes` set to `['hidden']`.

The menu action is not visible in the menu's list of actions. This is useful for temporarily hiding a menu action item. | | 4️⃣ — The fourth menu action is a "disabled" + "destructive" action.
Visually, it looks very similar to an action that has the `['disabled']` attribute. |

### `ContextMenuView` Example 15 **Summary**: Context Menu Previews — An example showing how to configure a context menu that uses targeted previews.
| Notes | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | By default, the child elements you render inside the `ContextMenuView` component will be used as the preview when the context menu interaction is triggered.

Targeted previews allows you to specify which specific view to use for the context menu preview, so that when the context menu interaction begins, a different view will be used for the preview (including the initial transition, see the gif below the example code).

📝 **Note A**: The context menu interaction will still be triggered by long pressing on the child elements in the `ContextMenuView` component.

As such, if the view that you are using for the targeted preview is not a child of `ContextMenuView`, then holding down on that view will not trigger the context menu interaction.

📝 **Note B**: Targeted previews is different from setting a [custom context menu preview](#ContextMenuView-Example-11) via the `renderPreview` prop.

A custom preview will replace the contents of the context menu preview entirely with your custom view component once the menu is opened.

A targeted preview on the other hand will change which view to use for the context menu entrance/exit transition (as well as what view to show in the preview if you do not have a custom preview). |
[🔗 Full Example](./example/src/examples/ContextMenuViewExample15.tsx) ```jsx // 📝 Note: for the sake of brevity, some of the code is omitted... import { ContextMenuView } from 'react-native-ios-context-menu'; export function ContextMenuViewExample15(props) { const [targetViewNode, setTargetViewNode] = React.useState(); React.useEffect(() => { // please note that when a view unmounts and remounts (e.g. // when you have a view inside a list comp)., you need to // get the new associated `reactTag` for that view // // otherwise the `reactTag` value you provide to the // `previewConfig` will be stale... // // this is why we have to set `targetViewNode` back to // `udefined` when the component unmounts return () => { setTargetViewNode(undefined); } }, []); return ( { setTargetViewNode(nativeEvent.target) })} > {`Hello! Target Node: ${targetViewNode}`} ); }; ``` ![screenshot](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample15-old.png) ![Gif](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample15.gif)

### `ContextMenuView` Example 19 **Summary**: Dynamic Menu — An example showing a context menu that shows a loading indicator using deferred menu elements.
| Notes | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1️⃣ — If you control your `ContextMenuView.menuConfig` via state, then you can already dynamically add menu items while the context menu is visible (See [`ContextMenuView` Example 10](#ContextMenuView-Example-10)). However, there is no indication in the UI that items are currently being loaded.

You can use a "deferred element" in order to add an action item that has a loading indicator. Once you are done loading the content, then you can replace the deferred element with the actual menu items that you want to add.

📝 **Note**: Deferred elements are only available on iOS 14 and above. | | 2️⃣ — As mentioned in the previous examples, the `MenuConfig.menuItems` property can accept an array of `MenuElementConfig` union type. This means that it can accept an array containing any of the following object types: `MenuConfig` object, `MenuActionConfig`, and `DeferredMenuElementConfig`.

If we pass in a `DeferredMenuElementConfig` to `menuItems`, it means that we want to create "deferred element" item. | | 3️⃣ — To create a deferred element, we just need to create a "config" object that has a property containing both `type` and `deferredID`.

The `DeferredMenuElementConfig.type` property must be set to a string value of `'deferred'`. This indicates that we want to create a deferred element.

The `DeferredMenuElementConfig.deferredID` property must be set to a unique string value. Since we can have multiple deferred elements, the value you pass into this property will be used to identify which deferred element will be replaced with the menu items you want to add when the loading is complete. | | 4️⃣ — Once the context menu is open, any deferred menu items in `MenuConfig.menuItems` will trigger the `ContextMenuView.onRequestDeferredElement` event to fire. Via the event, you will receive two arguments: `deferredID` string and `provider` callback function.

The `deferredID` string corresponds to which deferred element that we need to load, while the `provider` callback function is used to provide the menu items that we want to add and replace the deferred element with. | | 5️⃣ — The `provider` callback function accepts an array of `MenuElementConfig` items.

To replace the deferred element with the menu items you want add, simply call the `provider` callback function with the array of `MenuConfig`, `MenuActionConfig`, or `DeferredMenuElementConfig` objects.

📝 **Note A**: Since the deferred elements were loaded/replaced using the `onRequestDeferredElement` event, there are now two sources of truths for the context menu config: One provided via the `ContextMenuView.menuConfig` prop, and the other via the `onRequestDeferredElement` event.

If you are using a state-controlled menu config, see: [`ContextMenuView` Example 20](#ContextMenuView-Example-20).

📝 **Note B**: It is recommended that you cache the items you have loaded, and then combine them with the existing `menuConfig` once the menu has been closed. |
[🔗 Full Example](./example/src/examples/ContextMenuViewExample19.tsx) ```jsx // 📝 Note: for the sake of brevity, some of the code is omitted... export function ContextMenuViewExample19(props) { return ( { switch(deferredID) { case 'deferred-01': // dummy delay, wait for 1 second... await Helpers.timeout(1000); // provide the items to add to the context menu... provider([{ type: 'action', actionKey: 'action-02', actionTitle: 'Deferred Item 02', actionSubtitle: 'Deferred item...' }, { type: 'action', actionKey: 'action-03', actionTitle: 'Deferred Item 03', actionSubtitle: 'Deferred item...' }]); break; }; }} > {/** ... */} ); }; ``` ![example-ContextMenuViewExample19](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample19.jpg) ![example-ContextMenuViewExample19](./assets/example-ContextMenuViewExample19.gif)

pullRequests.title: fix: codegen not resolving package
pullRequests.body:
When trying to pod install, codegen fails with the following error:
```ts
error Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports" in node_modules/react-native-ios-context-menu/package.json
```

By adding `package.json` to the exports field the issue is resolved.

pullRequests.title: fix: build for macOS catalyst
pullRequests.body:
There are some iOS 16.0 availability checks, however they do not work for macOS catalyst.
Which is why I added these checks:
```
#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)
```
in front of ``#if swift(>=5.7)`` and ``@available(iOS 16, *)`` to be able to compile react-native apps for macOS catalyst

readme.text:
# Turborepo starter

This is an official Yarn v1 starter turborepo.

## What's inside?

This turborepo uses [Yarn](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/) as a package manager. It includes the following packages/apps:

### Apps and Packages

- `docs`: a [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) app
- `web`: another [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) app
- `ui`: a stub React component library shared by both `web` and `docs` applications
- `eslint-config-custom`: `eslint` configurations (includes `eslint-config-next` and `eslint-config-prettier`)
- `tsconfig`: `tsconfig.json`s used throughout the monorepo

Each package/app is 100% [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/).

### Utilities

This turborepo has some additional tools already setup for you:

- [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) for static type checking
- [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) for code linting
- [Prettier](https://prettier.io) for code formatting

### Build

To build all apps and packages, run the following command:

```
cd my-turborepo
yarn run build
```

### Develop

To develop all apps and packages, run the following command:

```
cd my-turborepo
yarn run dev
```

### Remote Caching

Turborepo can use a technique known as [Remote Caching](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/core-concepts/remote-caching) to share cache artifacts across machines, enabling you to share build caches with your team and CI/CD pipelines.

By default, Turborepo will cache locally. To enable Remote Caching you will need an account with Vercel. If you don't have an account you can [create one](https://vercel.com/signup), then enter the following commands:

```
cd my-turborepo
npx turbo login
```

This will authenticate the Turborepo CLI with your [Vercel account](https://vercel.com/docs/concepts/personal-accounts/overview).

Next, you can link your Turborepo to your Remote Cache by running the following command from the root of your turborepo:

```
npx turbo link
```

## Useful Links

Learn more about the power of Turborepo:

- [Pipelines](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/core-concepts/monorepos/running-tasks)
- [Caching](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/core-concepts/caching)
- [Remote Caching](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/core-concepts/remote-caching)
- [Filtering](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/core-concepts/monorepos/filtering)
- [Configuration Options](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/reference/configuration)
- [CLI Usage](https://turbo.build/repo/docs/reference/command-line-reference)

readme.text: # React Native Skia High-performance 2d Graphics for React Native using Skia [![CI](https://github.com/Shopify/react-native-skia/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Shopify/react-native-skia/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@shopify/react-native-skia.svg?style=flat)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shopify/react-native-skia) [![issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/shopify/react-native-skia.svg?style=flat)](https://github.com/shopify/react-native-skia/issues) Checkout the full documentation [here](https://shopify.github.io/react-native-skia). React Native Skia brings the Skia Graphics Library to React Native. Skia serves as the graphics engine for Google Chrome and Chrome OS, Android, Flutter, Mozilla Firefox and Firefox OS, and many other products. ## Getting Started [Installation instructions](https://shopify.github.io/react-native-skia/docs/getting-started/installation/) ## Contributing For detailed information on library development, building, testing, and contributing guidelines, please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](packages/skia/CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Graphite Skia has two backends: Ganesh and Graphite. Ganesh is the default backend. Graphite is available as an experimental preview in the `@next` distribution channel: ```sh yarn add @shopify/react-native-skia@next ``` **This is highly experimental and not recommended for production use.** Skia Graphite requires Android API Level 26 or above. If you prefer to build Skia yourself with Graphite support, you can do so with `SK_GRAPHITE=1 yarn build-skia`. React Native Skia automatically detects Graphite via a marker file included in the prebuilt libs.

pullRequests.title: fix: Drawings.h change command props from private to public
pullRequests.body:
I'm working on https://github.com/samuelScheit/react-native-skia-yoga and I'm extending and reusing the draw commands defined in Drawings.h.
However as the props of the draw cmds are private it fails with: ` error: 'props' is a private member of 'RNSkia::RectCmd'`

I want to be able to update the props to be able to dynamically recalculate the layout using yoga and set width/height of each node/cmd and need to be able to access the private props.

I've tried to use patch-package but that only works locally and not when I would publish `react-native-skia-yoga` as package and need this fix to be merged upstream.

pullRequests.title: fix: web paragraph styles not working
pullRequests.body: I've tried to use the paragraph api on the web, however the paragraph didn't render and show up on the canvas. After debugging I found out that `paragraph.getHeight()` returned `0` and the `style.textStyle.fontSize` was `-1` and `style.textStyle.fontFamilies` was undefined. I've tried to directly create the style using `new CanvasKit.ParagraphStyle(...)` and that returned a style object with correct fontSize/fontFamily and when used also returned the correct paragraph height. That means the issue lies in the `JsiSkParagraphStyle.toParagraphStyle()` function: https://github.com/Shopify/react-native-skia/blob/4a2d7afc0fa547aee9938a0339594b88c3618d20/packages/skia/src/skia/web/JsiSkParagraphStyle.ts#L7-L65 Inside of the `toParagraphStyle()` function I've changed the assignments from strutStyle to textStyle (except for `leading`, `forceStrutHeight` and `strutEnabled`) and also added some properties like `textDecoration`, `backgroundColor` and `shadows`. This fixed the issue and now the paragraph correctly renders: ```ts const paragraphBuilder = Skia.ParagraphBuilder.Make( { textStyle: { color: Skia.Color("red"), fontSize: 50, fontFamilies: ["Roboto"], decoration: TextDecoration.Underline, decorationColor: Skia.Color("green"), decorationStyle: TextDecorationStyle.Wavy, decorationThickness: 1, letterSpacing: 1, fontStyle: { slant: FontSlant.Italic, weight: FontWeight.Normal, width: FontWidth.Normal, }, shadows: [ { blurRadius: 10, color: Skia.Color("blue"), offset: { x: 10, y: 10 }, }, ], textBaseline: TextBaseline.Ideographic, }, }, fontManager ) ```

# emoji-mashup

[![npm version][npm-version-src]][npm-version-href]
[![npm downloads][npm-downloads-src]][npm-downloads-href]
[![Github Actions CI][github-actions-ci-src]][github-actions-ci-href]

Easily create & mashup custom emojis ♻️🥴

## Install


```sh
# Using npm
npm install emoji-mashup

# Using yarn
yarn add emoji-mashup
```


## Usage

### `createCustomEmoji({ base, mouth?, eyes?, special? })`

This method converts the given emojis and then creates an SVG as string which you can write and edit.

```js
const { createCustomEmoji } = require("emoji-mashup");

const newEmoji = { base: "🥴", mouth: "🥴", eyes: "💀", special: "🤕" };
var emojiCombined = createCustomEmoji(newEmoji);

// You receive a string with the svg data, in this example we write a file with that.
// You will generate a mashup of 🥴, 💀 & 🤕.
```

details.name: timetable-generator
details.description: Ultimate flexible agile timetable generator

readme.text:
## Resources (for a lecture):

-   Room
-   Teacher
-   Class
-   Student
-   Time
-   Subject

## Room:

-   ID
-   Name/description
-   Room types (generic, laboratory, kitchen, office)
-   Room size/number of places
-   Room occupancy (["xx:xx - xx:xx"])

## Time:

-   Additional time between the hours (switching room, break, ventilation, discussions)
-   Teachers/students need breaks when it is convenient (or at a fixed time)

## Teacher:

-   Name
-   Type (teacher, professor, external employee)
-   Subjects
-   Availability

## Students:

-   Name
-   classes/courses

## Action/query:

-   Is the resource available? (Teacher, room, class) for a period
-   Set/give priority
-   Set hard/soft constraint

## Example rules:

-   Teacher + class + student can only be in one room at the same time
-   Subject can only take place in a certain room
-   Subjects should be in a certain order during the week
-   Minimize time between the hours
-   Reduce walking time between different rooms/facilities

## Algorithm

A metaheuristic evolutionary algorithm for creating timetables

Variables (G = Generations, P = Population, T = Stop Threshold, S = Selection percentage, M = Mutation probability)

-   Loads all resources
-   Loads all rules and sorts them by priority
-   Repeat until no improvement in performance is found after T runs or the user manually stops
    -   Repeat G times:
        -   Repeat P times:
            -   Starts with a random table or takes the one of the previous run
            -   Assigns performance 0 to this run
            -   Execute every rule for every resource
                -   If the rule is fulfilled, its priority is added to the performance
                -   If the rule is violated, its priority is subtracted from the service
                -   If the rule is violated and it is absolutely necessary, the service is set to 0 and this cycle is ended
    -   Saves and sorts the results according to the performance of the runs
    -   Selection (S percent of the best runs are selected)
    -   Recombination (some entries are swapped for two of the selected runs)
    -   Mutation (some entries are swapped with a probability of M)
    -   Population (100% - S are also filled in randomly generated tables)

## Schema:

```json
[
	{
		"and": [
			{
				"or": [
					{
						"equals": "1==1"
					},
					{
						"equals": "1==0"
					}
				]
			},
			{
				"equals": "1==1"
			}
		]
	}
]
```

```json
{
	"ressources": {
		"lehrer": {}
	}
}
```

details.name: GykiSpace
details.description: GyKi Space Chat

licenseInfo.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

readme.text:
# Gyki Space

## Abstract
This protocol defines the protocol to communicate between the GykiSpace server and client over a text interface. This is Version 1 and there are no revisions planned. 

## Introduction
The server listens on port 8051 for connections and can handle multiple connections simultaneously. Each connections is handled in their own Thread and is waiting for events. Events are encoded as XML strings and sent as a single packet. When the client connects to the server over a TCP socket the server responds with an hello event, which returns metadata about the server. After that the client should send pings based on the ping_interval. If a server doesn't respond within 5 seconds on a ping the connection should be closed and a new one should be established. Subsequently the client sends the identify event and waits for the Ready event.

## Structures
Every event has a type key which uniquely identifies the event type.

### Hello Event
|     **Key**    | **Type** |                       **Description**                       |
|:--------------:|:--------:|:-----------------------------------------------------------:|
|      type      |     0    |                                                             |
|  online\_users |    int   |               Number of currently online users              |
| ping\_interval |    int   | How often the client should ping the server in milliseconds |

Possible future additions: icon, name

### Ping Event
**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|1| 

### Identify Event
**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|2| 
username|string|Minimum 2 char name of the connecting user

Possible future additions: avatar

### Ready Event

**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|3| 
rooms| |Array of rooms that are joinable

### Message Event
**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|4| 
content|String|Content of the message
sender|String|Username of the sender

Possible future additions: file

### Create Room Event
Sent by the client to create a new room

**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|5| 
name|String|Name of this message room
recipients|String[]|Array of usernames that should be added to the room
public|boolean|Whether or not the room should be publicly joinable by everyone

### Add Room Event
Received by the client if user was added to a room.

**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|6| 
name|String|Name of the room
recipients|String[]|Array of usernames that are in this room

### User Join Event
**Key**|**Type**|**Description**
:-----:|:-----:|:-----:
type|7| 
name|String|Name of the room
username|String|Name of the user that joined

Es macht keinen Sinn zu erwaehnen, dass dieser Text eigentlich gar keinen Sinn hat. Warum ist es mir ueberhaupt in den Sinn gekommen, einen Text zu schreiben, der absolut keinen Sinn hat? Womoeglich haette es einen Sinn, wenn ich mir einen ueberlegt haette. Wobei wenn ich ehrlich bin, macht es genauso wenig Sinn, einen Text mit Sinn zu nennen. Wie sinnlos waere das, dem Leser anzukuendigen, dass der Text einen Sinn hat. Nun faellt mir auf, dass es auch genauso wenig Sinn machen wuerde, diesen Text zu lesen, ich meine, wie sinnlos waere das? Es waere eine sinnlose Zeitverschwendung. Mit ebenso wenig Sinn, wie einen Text zu schreiben, den eigentlich man nicht zu lesen braucht, weil er diesen Sinnesanspruch einfach nicht gerecht wird. Und nun komme ich zu dem Schluss, dass ich mich noch sinnloserweise darueber aufregen koennte, wie sinnlos es ist, in allem immer einen Sinn sehen zu wollen. Es muss ja nun nicht wirklich immer alles einen Sinn ergeben. Waere ja sinnlos, wenn alles einen Sinn haette.

readme.text:
# Database Browser
## Archived

A simple Database-Browser in HTML, CSS, JS and PHP with which you can view and change MYSQL Databases

## Example

![Example](example.png)

## Getting Started

These instructions will get you a copy of the project up and running on your local machine for development and testing purposes.

### Prerequisites

You need to install the LAMP stack: https://www.linode.com/docs/web-servers/lamp/install-lamp-stack-on-ubuntu-16-04/

### Installing

To install it, enter these commands in your Terminal:

```
cd /var/www/html/
git clone https://github.com/Flam3rboy/Database-Browser.git
```

## Built With

-   [jQuery](http://jquery.com/) - JS Framework
-   [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/) - HTML, CSS, and JS library
-   [Material Design for Bootstrap](https://mdbootstrap.com/) -Theme for Bootstrap
-   [jQuery lined Textarea Plugin](http://alan.blog-city.com/jquerylinedtextarea.htm) - Lined Div
-   [Popper JS](https://popper.js.org/) - Poppers in Web Applications
-   [Sorttable](http://www.kryogenix.org/code/browser/sorttable/) - Sort HTML Tables

## Versioning

I use [GIT](https://git-scm.com/) for versioning. For the versions available, see the [commits on this repository](https://github.com/Flam3rboy/Database-Browser/commits/master).

## Authors

-   **Flam3rboy** - Student

readme.text:
# Commando
[![Discord](https://discordapp.com/api/guilds/222078108977594368/embed.png)](https://discord.gg/bRCvFy9)
[![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/discord.js-commando.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/discord.js-commando)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/discord.js-commando.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/discord.js-commando)
[![Dependency status](https://david-dm.org/discordjs/Commando.svg)](https://david-dm.org/discordjs/Commando)
[![Build status](https://github.com/discordjs/Commando/workflows/Testing/badge.svg)](https://github.com/discordjs/Commando/actions?query=workflow%3ATesting)

## About
Commando is the official command framework for [discord.js](https://github.com/discordjs/discord.js).
It is flexible, fully object-oriented, easy to use, and makes it trivial to create your own powerful commands.
Additionally, it makes full use of ES2017's `async`/`await` functionality for clear, concise code that is simple to write and easy to comprehend.

## Features
- Plain command names and aliases
- Regular expression triggers
- Robust parsing of arguments (with "quoted strings" support)
- Sophisticated argument system (optional)
	* Automatic prompting for arguments that aren't provided
	* Type system with rules, automatic validation, and parsing to usable values
		- Basic types (string, integer, float, boolean)
		- Discord objects (user, member, role, channel, message)
		- User-defined custom types
		- Union types
	* Automatic re-prompting of invalid arguments
	* Optional arguments with default values
	* Infinite arguments (arguments that accept as many values as provided)
- Multiple responses to commands
- Command editing (user edits their message that triggered the command, and the bot's response updates with it)
- Command reloading, as well as loading/unloading
- Command throttling/cooldowns

## Installation
**Node 12.0.0 or newer is required.**  
`npm install discord.js@12 discord.js-commando`

## Documentation
[View the docs here.](https://discord.js.org/#/docs/commando)  
See the [discord.js documentation](https://discord.js.org/#/docs) as well.

readme.text:
# React Native WebView

![star this repo](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/react-native-webview/react-native-webview?style=flat-square)
[![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg?style=flat-square)](http://makeapullrequest.com)
[![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react-native-webview.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-webview)
![Npm Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/react-native-webview.svg)

**React Native WebView** is a community-maintained WebView component for React Native. It is intended to be a replacement for the built-in WebView (which was [removed from core](https://github.com/react-native-community/discussions-and-proposals/pull/3)).

### Maintainers

**Many thanks to these companies** for providing us with time to work on open source.  
Please note that maintainers spend a lot of free time working on this too so feel free to sponsor them, **it really makes a difference.**

- [Thibault Malbranche](https://github.com/Titozzz) ([Twitter @titozzz](https://twitter.com/titozzz)) from [Brigad](https://www.brigad.co/en-gb/about-us)  
  [_Sponsor me_ ❤️ !](https://github.com/sponsors/Titozzz)

Windows and macOS are managed by Microsoft, notably:

- [Alexander Sklar](https://github.com/asklar) ([Twitter @alexsklar](https://twitter.com/alexsklar)) from [React Native for Windows](https://microsoft.github.io/react-native-windows/)
- [Chiara Mooney](https://github.com/chiaramooney) from [React Native for Windows @ Microsoft](https://microsoft.github.io/react-native-windows/)

Shout-out to [Jamon Holmgren](https://github.com/jamonholmgren) from [Infinite Red](https://infinite.red) for helping a lot with the repo when he had more available time.

### Disclaimer

Maintaining WebView is very complex because it is often used for many different use cases (rendering SVGs, PDFs, login flows, and much more). We also support many platforms.

Since WebView was extracted from the React Native core, nearly 500 pull requests have been merged.  
Considering that we have limited time, issues will mostly serve as a discussion place for the community, while **we will prioritize reviewing and merging pull requests.**

### Platform compatibility

This project is compatible with **iOS**, **Android**, **Windows** and **macOS**.  
This project only supports **the new architecture** (fabric); the legacy architecture (paper) is no longer supported. This requires **React Native 0.76 or newer** (with the new architecture enabled) and **iOS 15.1 or newer**; on macOS, react-native-macos 0.76 or newer.  
This project is compatible with [expo](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/webview/).

### Getting Started

Read our [Getting Started Guide](docs/Getting-Started.md). If any step seems unclear, please create a pull request.

### Versioning

This project follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/). We do not hesitate to release breaking changes but they will be in a major version.

### Usage

Import the `WebView` component from `react-native-webview` and use it like so:

```tsx
import React, { Component } from 'react';
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { WebView } from 'react-native-webview';

// ...
const MyWebComponent = () => {
  return (
    <WebView
      source={{ uri: 'https://reactnative.dev/' }}
      style={{ flex: 1 }}
    />
  );
};
```

For more, read the [API Reference](./docs/Reference.md) and [Guide](./docs/Guide.md). If you're interested in contributing, check out the [Contributing Guide](./docs/Contributing.md).

### Common issues

- If you're getting `Invariant Violation: Native component for "RNCWebView does not exist"` it likely means you forgot to run `react-native link` or there was some error with the linking process
- If you encounter a build error during the task `:app:mergeDexRelease`, you need to enable multidex support in `android/app/build.gradle` as discussed in [this issue](https://github.com/react-native-webview/react-native-webview/issues/1344#issuecomment-650544648)

#### Contributing

Contributions are welcome, see [Contributing.md](https://github.com/react-native-webview/react-native-webview/blob/master/docs/Contributing.md)

### License

MIT

### Translations

This readme is available in:

- [Brazilian portuguese](docs/README.portuguese.md)
- [French](docs/README.french.md)
- [Italian](docs/README.italian.md)

pullRequests.title: feat(napi): expose the main-process reset boundary
pullRequests.body: Expose the Rust runtime reset gate through the host-facing N-API surface so the main process can complete legacy cleanup before constructing RuntimeHandle.\n\nThe API accepts explicit platform-owned paths and delegates all validation and destructive work to respond-runtime, preserving the fail-closed absolute-path, duplicate, symlink, and regular-file checks. Notification extensions do not receive this write-capable entry point and remain marker-read-only.\n\nValidated with cargo fmt --all and cargo test -p respond-napi --all-targets (29 tests). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: docs(runtime): record reset and APNS cutover evidence
pullRequests.body: Document the concrete reset-gate implementation and its failure-safe marker semantics so the port checklist distinguishes the intended boundary from the shipped runtime. Record the APNS server boundary as implemented and point to the Rust/N-API, host-loading, Node/Bun, and worker validation already completed in the preceding stack layers. Keep all provider rows that lack a Rust acceptance suite explicitly incomplete. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(runtime): add atomic legacy reset gate
pullRequests.body: Introduce the main-process reset boundary required by the Rust runtime generation. The gate accepts only explicit absolute file paths, rejects broad targets and application-controlled symlink components, revokes stale authorization before a failed reset can return, removes the database and caller-listed legacy secure-storage artifacts, and publishes the reset-complete marker through a synced temporary file and atomic rename. Share the marker constants with respond-extension-ffi so extension authorization and main-app publication cannot drift. Add filesystem tests covering complete cleanup, idempotent re-execution, directory rejection, relative/root path rejection, symlink targets, marker contents, and the no-authorizing-marker failure invariant. Validation: cargo test -p respond-runtime --test reset_gate; cargo test -p respond-extension-ffi --all-targets; cargo test -p respond-runtime --all-targets. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: refactor(server): remove legacy TypeScript APNS protocol boundary
pullRequests.body: Make the Rust runtime the sole APNS protocol, credential, registration-key, and notification-normalization authority for the server surface. Replace the TypeScript certificate parser and MessagePack client/wire implementation with the direct N-API courier, including account-scoped opaque notification draining and the native registration-key contract. Remove duplicate protocol tests and relocate courier fixtures beside the Rust implementation, while preserving server-level registration and bridge coverage. Harden worker timer ownership, serialized notification draining, addon boundary validation, and platform payload adaptation so malformed native failures cannot leak secrets or race lifecycle cleanup.\n\nValidation: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-features; cargo build -p respond-napi --all-features; host-loading Node/Bun integration; server APNS bridge tests; bun run lint; focused anti-slop lint; git diff --check. The repository-wide TypeScript check retains only the pre-existing Bun/Hono websocket typing mismatch in server/src/Server.ts:83. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(server): move APNS courier boundary into Rust
pullRequests.body: ## Rust-owned APNS server boundary Move the APNS courier protocol, SHA-1 topic hashing, packet and command framing, certificate validation, TLS session lifecycle, notification decoding, provider normalization, and canonical registration identity into `respond-runtime` and expose it through the Node/Bun `respond-napi` addon. The TypeScript server now keeps only HTTP, Redis, BullMQ, and platform-delivery orchestration. It no longer imports `@respond/library`, instantiates the mobile runtime, or owns APNS credential material. Durable Redis state contains an operator credential reference only; Rust loads mounted certificate/key material into process memory and validates it before connecting. ## Breaking registration cutover Replace the retired four-field registration identity with strict server push generation 2. Registrations now require an explicit account, provider, remote-account, installation, APNS endpoint, environment, and push mode. The canonical Rust key includes every routing dimension while excluding rotating device tokens. The obsolete v1 key path and compatibility defaults are removed. ## Verification - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` - `cargo test --workspace --all-features` - `cargo build -p respond-napi --all-features` - `crates/respond-napi/tests/run-host-loading-server.sh` - `RESPOND_NAPI_SERVER_PATH=... bun test server/tests` (11 pass) - `bun run lint` - `git diff --check` `bunx tsc -p server/tsconfig.json --noEmit` remains blocked by the existing `server/src/Server.ts:83` Bun/Hono `websocket` typing mismatch; the APNS modules do not introduce an additional TypeScript error. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: fix(runtime): correlate attachment echoes by durable draft identity
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Replaces heuristic attachment echo matching with exact durable local attachment identities and atomically persisted provider receipts.

## Why

The former matcher selected a candidate from attachment metadata and event order. Two otherwise identical drafts could be swapped, provider-side metadata changes could prevent reconciliation, and retry/restart behavior had no durable local-to-remote mapping.

## What changed

- Remote attachment ingress accepts an adapter-proven client attachment key only when it matches the event account.
- Confirmed adapter executions carry exact attachment receipts. Storage requires complete command-owned coverage, rejects duplicate/reused identities, and writes the mappings with the outbox transition and journal batch.

pullRequests.title: fix(napi): release runtime resources on disposal
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Explicit `RuntimeHandle.dispose()` previously only fenced logical access. `RuntimeInner` permanently retained an `Arc<SqliteStore>`, so a JavaScript handle kept the SQLite/SQLCipher connection and its key-bearing store alive until garbage collection. Disposal also waited behind the mutation mutex, allowing a synchronous host-side teardown call to block behind native work.

This change makes runtime-owned resources explicit and detachable:

- Store the runtime lease and subscriber registry together in `RuntimeResources`, with the store represented as `Option<Arc<SqliteStore>>`.
- Mark the runtime unavailable first, then detach and drop its store lease without taking the long-running mutation fence.
- Require requests to acquire a short-lived local store lease only after the mutation fence and a second disposal check, returning typed `Unavailable` when disposal wins while work was queued.
- Add publication and terminal-loss gates so teardown cannot enqueue a fresh callback after its boundary.

A genuinely in-flight task may complete using its own temporary store lease; explicit disposal still releases the runtime-owned SQLCipher/key lease immediately. Callbacks already handed to the host event loop cannot be retracted and remain fenced by the TypeScript façade.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo build -p respond-napi --release`
- Node and Bun release-addon disposal smoke tests

- `actionlint .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/extension-ffi.yml`

The Rust coverage specifically proves prompt disposal while mutation is held, release of the runtime-owned store via `Weak<SqliteStore>`, typed rejection for queued requests, and retained-subscription teardown.

pullRequests.title: build(tooling): make the root Bun workspace authoritative
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Make the repository root the sole JavaScript dependency authority.

- Pin Node to `20.20.2` via `.nvmrc` and pin Bun to the published, reproducible `1.3.14` release in `packageManager`, GitHub Actions, Docker, documentation, and the regenerated root `bun.lock`.
- Consolidate workspace manifests, trusted lifecycle policy, and the six retained dependency patches at the root; delete nested Bun/Yarn locks, child patch-package trees, obsolete helper workspace files, and generated TypeScript metadata.
- Move the root, library, and server Dockerfiles to repository-root build contexts. Each installs from the same root manifest/lock, all workspace manifests, and patches before copying runtime source. `build.sh` uses those root contexts as well.
- Exclude host dependency trees, build output, caches, databases, logs, and environment files from every Docker context while retaining the workspace manifests Bun needs to resolve.
- Replace the stale Yarn-only library check with a Node/Bun workspace gate that freezes the root install, verifies lifecycle trust, resolves every explicit public `@respond/library` export under both hosts, and builds all three root-context images on Linux. The workflow watches live library/server source and every Docker/context input, not just manifests.
- Remove the invalid Trant mobile-release and Yarn Tauri publishing workflows. This intentionally retires broken release automation; it does **not** claim a replacement desktop release pipeline. Desktop remains outside the mobile/server Rust cutover until its dedicated adapter and release path are validated.
- Update contributor documentation to use one root frozen install and Bun filters.

## Why

A lockfile cannot be authoritative if CI, containers, build entry points, or documentation reconstruct dependency state from deleted child locks or an unpublished host-only Bun canary. One released Bun version plus one root lock makes the JavaScript dependency graph reproducible. Root-context Docker and CI checks make that authority continuously enforceable.

## Validation

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` — 3,169 packages checked with no lock changes
- `bun pm untrusted` — 0 untrusted lifecycle dependencies
- Node and Bun resolution of the root, APNS, Discord, Signal, WhatsApp, Demo, `Core/Providers`, and `db/drizzle` library exports
- stable-Bun server smoke: `GET /` returned `200 Online` with an intentionally unavailable Redis endpoint

## Stack position

This is a draft child of `codex/napi-subscription-loss` (PR #369), not of `main`. Its only parent commit is `f8440f9b`, and it intentionally contains one focused N-API callback-lifetime repair.

## Summary

A terminal subscriber failure keeps the one-shot loss callback alive until JavaScript receives it. That is necessary so the façade can initiate durable recovery, but the callback was never subsequently released. Bun then retained its event loop after an event callback failure.

This change releases the loss TSFN immediately after the queued JavaScript loss notification completes. The completion closure holds a `Weak<Subscriber>`, rather than an `Arc`, so callback queue teardown cannot create a self-retaining cycle. Explicit subscription disposal now always deactivates the token-owned subscriber, including after failure has already removed it from the runtime subscription registry.

## Guarantees preserved

- Event callback delivery remains bounded and terminal failures are reported at most once.
- The loss callback is not aborted before an ordinary queued notification can reach JavaScript.
- Failed queueing releases callback resources promptly.
- Explicit disposal or runtime teardown cancels any undeliverable callback work.
- The per-runtime mutation fence and lifetime-generation fencing remain unchanged.

pullRequests.body: ## Summary Define the provider synchronization contract needed by a Rust-owned account supervisor. Adapters now declare their immutable cursor namespaces, and every finite sync response explicitly reports whether more work remains or the stream is caught up. ## Correctness changes - Add `SyncProgress::MoreAvailable` and `SyncProgress::CaughtUp` to prevent supervisors from inferring readiness from an empty or short page. - Reject a `MoreAvailable` response that has no batches or fails to advance its complete opaque checkpoint. - Require adapters to expose a non-empty stream inventory instead of forcing every provider through a runtime-wide default cursor. - Add a shared stream-inventory validator for supervisor and adapter acceptance checks. - Document the stream/catch-up ownership boundary in the port checklist. ## Regression coverage - Prove empty caught-up responses are valid. - Reject unchanged cursor-only responses marked as having more work. - Accept an advancing cursor-only continuation. - Reject empty adapter stream inventories. - Update all existing sync validation fixtures to state progress explicitly. ## Verification - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo test -p respond-core --all-features --no-fail-fast` - `cargo clippy -p respond-core --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` - `git diff --check` --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: test(runtime): prove adapter session durability and fencing
pullRequests.body: ## Summary Add end-to-end SQLite coverage for the journaled adapter-session boundary and document the supervisor ownership rules in the porting checklist. ## Coverage - Identity installation, canonical account/person claims, ordered account batches, journal replay, encrypted reopen, and read-only snapshots. - Exact retained retries both before and after process restart, plus explicit compaction behavior that fences a retired receipt and requires resnapshot. - Valid lifecycle progression, illegal-edge rollback, stale expected-lifecycle rejection, lifecycle ABA protection, and old exact retries after later progress. - Fresh no-op reports advancing the durable journal generation so stale work cannot reuse the same expected position. - Immutable descriptor enforcement, monotonic identity preservation, rebinding rejection, account/person canonical-ID collisions, cross-account namespace isolation, and recovery after a rejected transaction. - Account-close fencing and a raw SQLite regression proving that an orphaned generic `adapter_state` row cannot forge a session retry receipt. ## Documentation Record that adapters have no raw SQL or generic account-write capability; a future Rust supervisor owns cancellation, submits session reports through the semantic store boundary, and resnapshots after compaction retires a replay receipt. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(runtime): add journaled adapter session boundary
pullRequests.body: ## Summary Introduce the durable supervisor-to-store boundary for adapter lifecycle and verified identity reports. This replaces the unused authentication result with an explicit `AdapterSession` / `AdapterSessionUpdate` contract and gives Rust runtime supervisors one atomic operation for reconciling provider state. ## Durable behavior - Validate an adapter descriptor against the bootstrapped account’s immutable provider, profile, and capability configuration. - Merge verified account and self-person remote identities monotonically: omitted values preserve facts, while rebinding is rejected. - Fence stale asynchronous work with both the observed journal sequence and expected lifecycle, including lifecycle ABA cycles. - Reject adapter attempts to target `idle` or `closed`; account closure stays on the account-action path so outbox cancellation and wipe fencing cannot be bypassed. - Claim canonical remote identities, update the account projection, and append one account change in the same immediate SQLite transaction. ## Replay integrity Every accepted report—including a projection no-op—advances the journal. The complete session update is retained as optional provenance inside that same one-account journal batch, making exact replay evidence inseparable from the committed account projection. Retained exact retries are no-ops; after journal compaction removes the receipt, retries fail with `Conflict` and supervisors must resnapshot. This removes the former shadow-fence design and its unbounded independent state. ## Binding contract Expose synchronous and async store entry points, validate the resulting session batch exactly, and map invalid adapter-session errors to the typed N-API invalid-command boundary. The new operation remains internal to Rust supervisors; JavaScript cannot send adapter-owned session updates. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: fix(runtime): enforce canonical remote identities
pullRequests.body: ## Summary - Establish an account-scoped canonical remote-ID registry with typed ownership claims for accounts, projections, relationship references, future tombstones, local completion binding, rollback restoration, and account descriptors. - Reject cross-kind reuse both while validating a normalized remote batch and while persisting transactional ingress, then enforce the invariant structurally with projection and descriptor composite foreign keys. - Make the SQLCipher storage boundary reset-only: use a runtime-specific storage version and SQLite application ID, verify the complete schema manifest, reject prototype or foreign layouts, and document the required platform reset gate. - Eliminate writable-open admission races by configuring SQLCipher before page access, admitting the final connection under an exclusive lock, verifying or initializing the layout while locked, and preserving normal multi-connection behavior after release. - Split opaque exact reaction tombstone IDs from synthetic actor/emoji tuple markers, retain typed tombstone claims, persist the exact-to-tuple companion relationship, and fail closed on malformed, missing, or mismatched durable companions. - Retire linked exact reaction tombstones whenever their tuple is superseded by ordered remote ingress, an id-less echo, a new explicit reaction ID, or a local optimistic re-add, without conflating opaque provider IDs with tuple marker values. ## Coverage - Add canonical-ID batch, projection, descriptor, future-tombstone, and completion collision coverage. - Add SQLCipher storage marker, schema-manifest, WAL-artifact, concurrent admission, writable/read-only reopen, and raw-corruption coverage. - Add reaction namespace collision tests in both arrival orders, independent marker clearing, companion corruption rejection, and id-less/new-ID/local re-add lifecycle regressions. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --check` - `git diff --check` - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` - `cargo test -p respond-runtime --test sqlite_store --no-fail-fast` (85 passed) - `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.body: ## Summary Establish the iOS side of the direct Rust notification FFI proof without wiring a partial production notification implementation. - add the Xcode build-phase entry point that compiles the checked-in respond-extension-ffi Cargo static library for the active device or simulator architecture - cover arm64 device output plus a universal arm64 and x86_64 simulator archive, including the iOS 16 deployment target - compile and execute an Objective-C++ host against the checked-in C ABI, checking ABI compatibility, typed malformed-request fallback ownership, and output-slot clearing - make the build script resilient to Xcode's reduced PATH while preserving an explicit CARGO_BIN override - record the acceptance evidence and explicitly document that secure bootstrap, provider parsing, native content mapping, and legacy Hermes removal remain later cutover work ## Validation - sh -n client/ios/scripts/build-respond-extension-ffi.sh - sh -n client/ios/scripts/test-respond-extension-ffi.sh - client/ios/scripts/test-respond-extension-ffi.sh - xcodebuild -project client/ios/respond.xcodeproj -list - cargo fmt --all -- --check - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast - git diff --check The full notification target is intentionally not claimed as built here: this clean worktree has no client/ios/Pods directory, while the standalone native acceptance gate is deliberately independent of CocoaPods and the legacy Hermes target. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: test(extension): verify JNI host boundary
pullRequests.body:
## Stack

This is the next layer in the Rust notification-extension proof stack. Its direct base is `codex/rust-extension-ffi-proof` ([#355](https://github.com/respondchat/respond/pull/355)).

## Summary

- add a checked-in Java fixture for the documented static, non-overloaded `NativeNotificationProcessor.process` JNI boundary;
- compile it with `javac -h` and assert the generated descriptor, symbol, static receiver, and argument order;
- load Cargo's actual release `cdylib` through `System.load`, invoke the real Rust JNI export, and decode its MessagePack results in Rust;
- cover malformed, null, oversized, and invalid-key calls as nonempty typed `malformed_request` fallbacks; and
- document the release host-smoke command and JDK requirement beside the extension FFI checks.

## Why

The existing Rust helper tests prove conversion semantics, but they cannot prove that a JVM can locate and call the exported native symbol with the exact host declaration. This layer exercises the complete Java-to-JNI-to-Rust boundary without introducing N-API, Hermes, React Native, or an Android service dependency.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p respond-extension-ffi --test jni_host_smoke -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test -p respond-extension-ffi --release --test jni_host_smoke -- --nocapture`
- `cargo clippy -p respond-extension-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p respond-extension-ffi --all-targets --all-features --no-fail-fast`

pullRequests.title: feat(extension): add direct notification FFI proof
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Adds the isolated direct native notification-extension proof in `respond-extension-ffi`. The crate produces a static library and cdylib for iOS C consumers and Android JNI consumers without N-API, Hermes, React Native, or JavaScript dependencies.

## What changed

- Adds a strict versioned MessagePack request and response protocol with bounded payloads, exact decoding, and typed safe fallback results.
- Adds shared reset-gated SQLCipher notification processing for deterministic Demo fixture pushes.
- Adds the C ABI, checked header, slot-clearing response ownership contract, and documented generic fallback behavior for all non-OK statuses.
- Adds the Android JNI export with pre-copy bounds, pending-exception cleanup, and zeroized copied key material.
- Guards direct Rust use with bounded absolute native paths, no-follow reset marker access, deadline budgeting, lock fallback, and read-only artifact stability checks.

## Verification

- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy -p respond-extension-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p respond-extension-ffi --all-targets --all-features --no-fail-fast
- cargo build -p respond-extension-ffi --release
- C11 and C++17 header syntax checks with warnings treated as errors
- Release export and forbidden-native-dependency inspection
- Disposable JVM load and JNI invocation proof

## Deliberate proof boundary

This change does not yet integrate platform notification services, platform secure-storage acquisition, or real-provider decryption/readiness. The next stacked host-smoke slice will check in the JVM signature/load/invoke coverage.

pullRequests.title: feat(runtime): add bounded read-only SQLCipher opens
pullRequests.body: Add a dedicated ReadOnlySqliteStore for notification-extension inspection of the Rust-owned database. The new path requires an existing regular file, opens SQLite with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY, applies the caller's busy deadline before encrypted-page access, verifies the exact v1 schema and foreign-key integrity without DDL or WAL initialization, and exposes only coherent account snapshot reads. Share the snapshot transaction helper with the writable store so read semantics stay identical without duplicating projection logic. Add regression coverage for missing-file non-creation, incomplete-schema non-initialization, unchanged schema snapshots, account-not-found behavior, and immediate lock fallback under a zero deadline. This closes the storage-resurrection and extension-deadline hazards before any direct C/JNI notification bridge can be layered on top. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: test(napi): verify Node and Bun addon boundaries
pullRequests.body: ## Summary - document the versioned handle, error-first callbacks, disposal semantics, replay handshake, and bounded synchronous-call policy - add a host-level CommonJS smoke fixture that drives the actual named MessagePack wire contract without a JavaScript domain model - exercise synchronous calls, Promise dispatch, callback ordering, idempotent command retries, callback failures, subscription loss, explicit disposal, runtime recreation, malformed bytes, trailing bytes, unsupported versions, and disposed-handle errors - verify the same release cdylib loads as a conventional addon file with the .node suffix in both Node and Bun - capture the host lifetime rule that a façade must close its own delivery gate before disposal because an already-dispatched callback cannot be retracted by every Node-API host ## Why Rust unit tests cannot prove addon loading, JavaScript callback marshalling, Promise resolution, or host-specific teardown behavior. This keeps those failure modes executable and documents the recovery contract the future reactive façade must implement. ## Verification - cargo fmt --all -- --check - cargo clippy -p respond-core -p respond-runtime -p respond-napi --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast - cargo build -p respond-napi --release - node smoke fixture against a copied addon file - bun smoke fixture against the same copied addon file --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(napi): add SQLCipher runtime bridge
pullRequests.body: ## Summary - turn the N-API crate into a keyed SQLCipher-backed RuntimeHandle rather than an empty addon target - expose one versioned MessagePack boundary through synchronous calls and libuv-backed Promises - return typed wire errors for malformed envelopes, command failures, conflicts, missing accounts, and disposed runtimes - serialize synchronous and asynchronous mutation publication behind one fence so callback batches retain commit order - use a bounded error-first ThreadsafeFunction callback path with explicit lost-subscription state on callback failure or queue pressure - add disposable runtime and subscription lifecycles, generation fencing, finalizer disposal, and queued-callback teardown - publish only newly committed command batches, never an idempotent response replay - enable portable dynamic N-API symbols and the rlib build required by binding tests and conventional Node/Bun addon loading ## Why This is the production-shaped host proof required before attaching application/provider behavior. It gives React Native Node-API, Node, and Bun a small owned runtime boundary with no legacy JSI, Hermes, globals, or JavaScript persistence path. ## Verification - cargo fmt --all -- --check - cargo clippy -p respond-core -p respond-runtime -p respond-napi --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast - cargo build -p respond-napi --release - Node and Bun native-addon smoke tests --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.body: ## Summary - add bounded synchronous entry points for account snapshots, journal replay, command admission, remote batch application, and virtual Combined queries - route the async Store Combined query through the same implementation so bindings and adapters cannot drift - make synchronous command admission return an explicit committed witness alongside the stable accepted-command fact - preserve exact idempotency retries while distinguishing them from a transaction that appended a fresh journal batch - validate restored accepted-command payloads with the strengthened shared core validator before returning them ## Why A Node-API host must not create an implicit async runtime just to perform short SQLite operations. It also must publish callback batches only for transactions committed by the current invocation; an idempotent retry is a durable response replay, not a new event. ## Verification - cargo fmt --all -- --check - cargo clippy -p respond-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test -p respond-runtime --test sqlite_store synchronous_command_acceptance_reports_only_new_durable_commits -- --exact - cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast - release Node and Bun addon smoke tests --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(runtime): add SQLCipher transactional store
pullRequests.body: ## Summary - Add the first Rust-owned SQLCipher SQLite storage vertical slice, including account-scoped relational projections, transactional journal persistence, and strict v1 schema admission. - Persist optimistic commands, idempotency records, outbox leases/retries, rollback images, stream-scoped checkpoints, processed remote events, and lifecycle fences. - Reconcile remote echoes by command-specific stable identity and fence stale provider completions with same-event and stream-causal tombstones. - Reject raw durable corruption before it can reach a provider call or silently normalize during a worker completion. ## Commit structure 1. `feat(runtime): add SQLCipher transactional store` — runtime implementation and durable integrity boundaries. 2. `test(runtime): verify SQLCipher storage boundaries` — public-port integration coverage for encryption, schema admission, journal replay, remote ingress, optimistic outbox work, corruption, tombstones, and account lifecycle behavior. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo check -p respond-runtime` - `cargo test -p respond-runtime --no-fail-fast` (57 integration tests) - `cargo test -p respond-runtime --test sqlite_store --no-fail-fast` - `cargo clippy -p respond-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` - `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` - `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` - `cargo doc -p respond-core --no-deps` - `git diff --check` Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

pullRequests.title: feat(runtime): define account-scoped core contracts
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

This is the second draft PR in the Rust runtime rewrite stack. It is intentionally based on `codex/rust-runtime-plan` (PR #345), not `main`.

Replace the build-only `respond-core` placeholder with the platform-neutral contract that the SQLCipher runtime, native bridges, provider adapters, and JavaScript façade will share.

## What this establishes

- Nominal, non-empty local IDs and account-scoped keys for every durable entity.
- Account-scoped remote identities, cross-account validation, and typed tombstones.
- Stable provider wire values, including the persisted `whatsapp` spelling.
- Discord-compatible provider profiles for Fosscord instead of a provider subclass/kind.
- Typed lifecycle states and transition validation with a terminal `closed` state.
- Typed capability policy that separates local archive/pin/mute/read behavior from remote provider mutations; RSS is read-only for remote messaging while local state remains available.
- Complete command families for messages, reactions, attachments, conversation preferences, read state, calls, and account lifecycle.
- Structured command requests, account-scoped idempotency, durable outbox states, leases, typed adapter results, retry policy, and terminal failures.
- Explicit provider sync streams, cursors, ordered remote event batches, de-duplication records, and atomic remote-apply/store ports.
- Account-scoped monotonic journal ranges, replay-or-snapshot-required semantics, per-account bootstrap snapshots, and a virtual Combined inbox query.
- Strict versioned MessagePack envelopes. The outer `kind` tag remains separate from nested `type` tags, schema/wire versions are validated, and trailing bytes are rejected.

## Verification

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p respond-core
cargo clippy -p respond-core --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
git diff --check
```

All pass locally. The 11 core tests are deterministic and cover stable serialization, nested envelope round trips, account isolation, idempotency, RSS capability behavior, lifecycle transitions, journal/snapshot scope, and retry policy boundaries.

## Deliberately not included

This PR does not claim SQLCipher implementation, provider protocol ports, N-API/FFI lifecycle proof, mobile packaging/device validation, or TypeScript façade migration. Those are subsequent stacked review units.

readme.text:
Spacebar Server

## [About](https://spacebar.chat) Spacebar/server is a Discord backend re-implementation and extension. We aim to reverse engineer and add additional features to the Discord backend, while remaining completely backwards compatible with existing bots, applications, and clients. This repository contains: - [API Request/Response Types](/src/schemas) - [Spacebar HTTP API Server](/src/api) - [WebSocket Gateway Server](/src/gateway) - [HTTP CDN Server](/src/cdn) - [WebRTC Server](/src/webrtc) - [Utility and Database Models](/src/util) - [Spacebar Admin API (C#)](/extra/admin-api) (Emma [it/its]@Rory& was here) ## [Documentation](https://docs.spacebar.chat) And with documentation on how to set up your own server [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/server), docs to set up either client [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/clients/), and docs about bots [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/bots/) ## [Contributing](https://docs.spacebar.chat/contributing/) ## Clients You _should_ be able to use any client designed for Discord.com to connect to a Spacebar instance. However, some incompatibilities still exist between Spacebar and Discord. For this reason, not every client will connect. We recommend using [Fermi](https://fermi.chat/login?instance=https%3A%2F%2Fspacebar.chat) as a solid starting point on your adventure in the SpaceBar!

This repository contains: - [API Request/Response Types](/src/schemas) - [Spacebar HTTP API server](/src/api) - [WebSocket Gateway server](/src/gateway) - [HTTP CDN server](/src/cdn) - [WebRTC server](/src/webrtc) - [Utility and Database Models](/src/util) - [Spacebar Admin API (C#)](/extra/admin-api/Spacebar.AdminApi) - [HTTP CDN server (C#)](/extra/admin-api/Spacebar.Cdn) - [Various other C# utilities](/extra/admin-api) ## [Documentation](https://docs.spacebar.chat) And with documentation on how to set up your own server [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/server), docs to set up either client [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/clients/), and docs about bots [here](https://docs.spacebar.chat/setup/bots/) ## [Contributing](https://docs.spacebar.chat/contributing/) ## Clients You _should_ be able to use any client designed for Discord.com to connect to a Spacebar instance. However, some incompatibilities still exist between Spacebar and Discord. For this reason, not every client will connect. We recommend using [Fermo](https://fermo.sovr.top/login?instance=spacebar.chat) as a solid starting point on your adventure in the SpaceBar! You can explore other clients with the [Spacebar Explorer](https://spacebar-explorer.sovr.top/clients).

pullRequests.title: Add joined private archived thread listing
pullRequests.body:
## Summary
- add `GET /channels/:channel_id/users/@me/threads/archived/private`
- filter archived private child threads to only those joined by the requesting guild member
- return Discord-compatible thread member objects for the current user and `has_more` pagination
- cover query construction, limit/before parsing, pagination, permissions, and member serialization with node:test

## Root cause
The server had thread creation/member APIs but no route for listing archived private threads joined by the current user, so clients could not page through their joined private archived threads for a parent channel.

Closes #125

## Validation
- `npm run node:tests`
- `npm run build:src -- --pretty false`
- `node -r dotenv/config -r module-alias/register --enable-source-maps --test dist/api/util/utility/JoinedPrivateArchivedThreads.test.js`
- `npx eslint src/api/routes/channels/#channel_id/users/@me/threads/archived/private.ts src/api/util/utility/JoinedPrivateArchivedThreads.ts src/api/util/utility/JoinedPrivateArchivedThreads.test.ts`
- `npx prettier --check src/api/routes/channels/#channel_id/users/@me/threads/archived/private.ts src/api/util/utility/JoinedPrivateArchivedThreads.ts src/api/util/utility/JoinedPrivateArchivedThreads.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

pullRequests.title: Support typed burst reactions
pullRequests.body:
## Summary
- support Discord's typed normal/burst reaction mutation routes
- track normal and burst users independently for each reaction emoji
- expose `count_details`, `me_burst`, and `burst_colors` in reaction responses while keeping legacy `user_ids` as normal reaction storage
- honor reaction `type` for add/remove gateway events and report the removed reaction owner's user id

## Root cause
The reaction route accepted or emitted a reaction type in some paths, but persisted all users for an emoji in a single untyped `user_ids` bucket. That made burst and normal reactions for the same emoji indistinguishable and caused idempotency, listing, removal, and gateway event payloads to collapse to the old normal-reaction behavior.

Fixes #999.

## Validation
- `npm run build`
- `npm run node:tests`
- `npm run lint` (passes with existing deprecation warnings in `src/util/util/Token.ts`)
- `git diff --check`

pullRequests.title: Resolve connection callback schema TODO
pullRequests.body:
## Summary
- type the connection callback `openid_params` payload as a string-valued OpenID parameter map
- add callback schema coverage for required fields, optional flags, `two_way_link_code`, top-level extra-property rejection, and string-only OpenID params
- preserve non-false `additionalProperties` in generated OpenAPI components so dictionary schemas remain typed

## Root cause
`ConnectionCallbackSchema.openid_params` was `unknown`, so JSON schema validation and generated docs did not describe or enforce the OpenID callback parameter map. The OpenAPI generator also deleted every top-level `additionalProperties`, which erased map value types after schema generation.

## Validation
- `npm run build`
- `node -r dotenv/config -r module-alias/register --enable-source-maps --test dist/schemas/uncategorised/ConnectionCallbackSchema.test.js`
- `npm run node:tests`
- `npm run lint` (passes with existing deprecation warnings in `src/util/util/Token.ts`)

Refs #1604

pullRequests.title: Type C# channel kinds
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

- Add a shared C# `ChannelType` enum for the DB `Channel.Type` model, aligned with Discord/Spacebar channel IDs.
- Replace Admin API/Offload channel-type magic-number checks with named enum values.
- Add .NET model tests covering enum values, typed entity usage, EF query behavior, and Npgsql integer-column mapping.

## Root cause

The Admin API TODO came from raw integer channel-kind checks (`1` for DM, `2` for guild voice). Keeping `Channel.Type` as an `int` allowed more magic-number drift; typing the DB model at the source keeps all C# callers on the same channel-kind contract while preserving the existing integer database column.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`
- `dotnet test extra/admin-api/Tests/Spacebar.Models.Db.Tests/Spacebar.Models.Db.Tests.csproj --artifacts-path /tmp/spacebar-channel-type-test --nologo --verbosity minimal`

Addresses the channel-type enum TODO from #1610.

pullRequests.title: Fix role member bulk update semantics
pullRequests.body:
## Summary
- add explicit `PUT /guilds/:guild_id/roles/:role_id/members` replacement semantics while keeping `PATCH` additive-only
- validate `member_ids` with a shared `RoleMembersUpdateSchema` and expose it in generated schema/OpenAPI output
- add focused regression tests for helper semantics, route wiring, and schema validation

## Root cause
The old `PATCH` route used a single `arrayPartition(...)` across all guild members and treated every non-addition as a removal. That meant omitted current holders were removed, listed holders could still fall into the remove set, and unrelated non-holders still hit `removeRole` calls.

## Validation
- `npm run build:src:tsgo`
- `npm run generate:schema`
- `npm run generate:openapi`
- `npm run node:tests`

Closes #445.

Rewrote the entire server to typeorm
Rate Limit
pullRequests.body:
A rate limit function that receives these parameters:
```ts
{
	bucket?: string; // pre defined bucket id, else just use request path 
	window: number; // timespan 
	count: number; // number of request in window/timespan
	bot?: number; // different number of requests for bots
	error?: number;// different number of requests for errors
	webhook?: number; // different number of requests for webhooks
	oauth?: number; // different number of requests for oauth applications
	GET?: number; // different number of requests for get routes
	MODIFY?: number; // different number of requests for any modify request method (e.g. POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
}
```
and returns a middleware function

Notice this rate limit doesn't increase the latency of requests, as it saves a local cache only of offenders through mongodb change streams and increments the hit count _after_ the request has been answered.
